MUQATIL:36:66-69/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:66-69/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:36:66-69/r3.claim: A person given long life is reversed in creation, becoming weaker; people should reason from this.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p817#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p817#2/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p817#2/r2.claim: Granting someone long life means bringing him to decrepit old age.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p817#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p817#2/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p817#2/r3.claim: Being turned back in creation means becoming like a child who cannot reason; Yaḥyā links this to 22:5, where some are returned to extreme old age and know nothing after knowledge.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p817#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p817#2/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p817#2/r4.claim: He argues that the One who created people, made them young and old, then returned them to childlike incapacity is able to resurrect them on Judgment Day.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p817#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p817#2/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p817#2/r5.claim: The people addressed by ‘do they not reason’ are the polytheists.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p145#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p145#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p145#4/r1.claim: Qatada describes aging as decline in hearing, sight, and strength.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p368#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p368#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p368#2/r1.claim: Making a person live long until he is reversed in creation means returning him to frail old age.

ZAJJAJ:v4p293/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p293/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p293/r3.claim: The word has several patterns derived from نكس; long life reverses creation from strength and youth to weakness and old age.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p543/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p543/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p543/r1.claim: These readers use yāʾ in أفلا يعقلون; Nāfiʿ and a report from Abū ʿAmr use tāʾ.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p543/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p543/r2.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو في رواية عباس بن الفضل
IBNMUJAHID:v1p543/r2.claim: Nāfiʿ and a report from Abū ʿAmr through ʿAbbās b. al-Faḍl use أفلا تعقلون with tāʾ.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200/r1.claim: Qatadah explains the reversal in old age through declining hearing, sight, and strength.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200/r2.speaker: سفيان
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200/r2.claim: Sufyan gives eighty years as the age meant by the verse.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200/r3.claim: Qatadah says extending a person's life brings senility, so after knowledge the person may know nothing.

NAHHAS:v3p403/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p403/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p403/r8.claim: God changes strength into weakness and youth into old age.

NAHHAS:v3p403/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p403/r9.speaker: عاصم والأعمش وحمزة
NAHHAS:v3p403/r9.claim: They read nunakkis-hu with intensive kāf; the light form has the same sense and can apply to little or much.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p45/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p45/r1.speaker: حمزة
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p45/r1.claim: Ḥamzah reads ننكسه with a doubled k, while ʿĀṣim's transmissions are mixed: most cited transmitters double it, but Hubayrah and ʿAlī ibn Naṣr report a light k.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p45/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p45/r2.speaker: قتادة
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p45/r2.claim: Qatādah explains the reversal as aging until a person knows nothing after having knowledge.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p45/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p45/r3.speaker: غيره
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p45/r3.claim: Another explanation is that prolonged life turns strength into weakness and youth into old age.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p45/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p45/r4.speaker: أبو الحسن
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p45/r4.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan calls ننكسه ordinary Arabic usage; he says نكسته is usually reserved for turning something upside down, and another authority reports that Abū ʿAmr rejected this form.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p46/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p46/r1.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p46/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr in the transmission from ʿAbbās read أفلا تعقلون in the second person, addressing the hearers.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p46/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p46/r2.speaker: الباقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p46/r2.claim: The other readers use the third-person أفلا يعقلون, meaning, 'Tell them: do they not reason?'; the second person continues the address in the preceding verse.

SULAMI:v2p174#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p174#2/r1.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
SULAMI:v2p174#2/r1.claim: A life spent in heedlessness is altered by each age until decline, but one enlivened by remembrance is unaffected by changing states and lives through nearness to the Real.

THALABI:v8p135/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p135/r2.speaker: الأعمش وعاصم وحمزة
THALABI:v8p135/r2.claim: They read ننكسه with a doubled consonant; other readers use the lighter form.

THALABI:v8p135/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p135/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p135/r3.claim: A long life returns a person to decrepit age like infancy, reversing strength, increase, sharpness, and freshness into weakness, decline, and decay.

THALABI:v8p135/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p135/r4.speaker: سفيان
THALABI:v8p135/r4.claim: He says the body changes when a person reaches eighty.

THALABI:v8p135/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p135/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p135/r5.claim: The question asks whether people will reason about this reversal in the created order.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r1.speaker: سفيان
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r1.claim: A long life may mean reaching eighty years.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r3.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r3.claim: God reverses people into weakness until they know nothing.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r4.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r4.claim: Alternatively, He changes their hearing, sight, and strength.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r5.claim: In creation may mean all created beings, as whoever is aged among them is reversed in creation.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r6.claim: Alternatively, a person's strength, youth, and growth turn into weakness, old age, and decline.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r7.claim: This should make people reason that the One who does this can resurrect them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r1.claim: The verb is also read with doubled consonant; the author cites several conjugated forms of نكس and refers to 21:65 for the root's meaning.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r2.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash says ننكسه is standard Arabic; نكسته is rarely used except for turning something over so its head becomes its feet.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r3.claim: Muqatil explains the verb as reaching old age.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r4.claim: Abu Ishaq says whoever is given a long life is reversed in form, changing from strength to weakness and youth to senility.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r5.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r5.claim: Qatada explains it as senility, when eyesight and strength change; this applies to everyone who grows old.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r6.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi says senility can return a person to the uncomprehending state of childhood; Qatada also reports that one who knew comes to know nothing.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r7.claim: The author says this mental deterioration is not universal, because not everyone who lives long reaches cognitive decline.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas, in Ata's report, restricts the verse to disbelievers and says God returns them to loss of reason, like the disbelievers in 95:5.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p515/r9.claim: On Ibn Abbas's view reversal means movement from knowledge to ignorance; the general view means strength to weakness, youth to gray hair, and increase to decrease.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p517/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p517/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p517/r1.claim: The rebuke asks why they do not reason: the One who changes human conditions can also raise people after death.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p517/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p517/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p517/r2.claim: A reading with تاء is explained by the address in 36:60.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:66-70/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:66-70/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:66-70/r3.claim: Long life reverses a person's condition: strength becomes weakness and youth becomes old age.

JISHUMI:v8p5896/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5896/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5896/r4.claim: Naks is turning something onto its head; related senses include breech birth, relapse in illness, and reversing an arrow.

JISHUMI:v8p5896/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5896/r6.speaker: عاصم، حمزة
JISHUMI:v8p5896/r6.claim: Asim and Hamza read ننكسه with a doubled kaf, damma on the first nun and fatha on the second; al-A'mash matches them. Others use a light kaf and a different vowel pattern.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p26/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p26/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p26/r1.claim: ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read ننكسه with doubling; the others read it lightly, meaning return to weak old age like a child.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p26/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p26/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p26/r2.claim: Another interpretation is that limbs weaken after strength and return to decline.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p26/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p26/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p26/r3.claim: The One who changes human conditions can resurrect the dead.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p460#4/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p460#4/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p460#4/r10.claim: God reverses an aged person from strength to weakness and from understanding toward foolishness, showing that only God can do this.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p460#4/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p460#4/r11.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p460#4/r11.claim: Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr read taʿqilūn, addressing the listeners; the remaining reciters read yaʿqilūn, speaking of absent people.

TABRISI:36:66-69/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:66-69/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:36:66-69/r2.claim: Some reciters pronounce nunakkis-hu with a doubled, kasra-marked kāf, while others use the lighter form; doubling can indicate repetition or intensity.

TABRISI:36:66-69/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:66-69/r8.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:36:66-69/r8.claim: Growing very old reverses a person’s bodily development: strength, size, freshness, and knowledge decline toward a condition like childhood.

TABRISI:36:66-69/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:66-69/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:36:66-69/r9.claim: The decline of old age should make people reason that the one who made them this way can also bring them back to life.

RAZI-FULL:v26p91#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p91#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p91#2/r1.claim: After warning had already cut off one excuse, God answers the claim that more worldly time would have prevented negligence: aging brings increasing weakness, so they wasted the period of ability and would not act in senility either.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r10.speaker: سفيان
QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r10.claim: At eighty a person's body changes and strength weakens.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r11.claim: A poem says time wears away a person's freshness and the two trusted faculties, hearing and sight.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r12.claim: Long life usually turns youth into old age, strength into weakness, and increase into decline.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r13.claim: The Prophet sought refuge from being returned to decrepit old age; Qurtubi says its explanation was given in al-Naḥl.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r14.claim: The point is that the One who ages people this way can resurrect them.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r15.speaker: نافع وابن ذكوان
QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r15.claim: They read the concluding verb with second-person tāʾ; the others read it with yāʾ.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r7.speaker: عاصم وحمزة
QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r7.claim: They read nunakkis-hu with a doubled kāf and ḍamma on the first nūn, from the form meaning to invert repeatedly.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r8.claim: The other reading has fatḥa on the first nūn and ḍamma on kāf, from nakasa, to turn something upside down.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r9.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:36:67-68/r9.claim: He explains the aging person's condition as resembling childhood.

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:68-69/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:68-69/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:68-69/r1.claim: As life is lengthened, bodily structure and powers progressively weaken in reverse of development; this gradual reversal includes the powers involved in transformation.

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:68-69/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:68-69/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:68-69/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir lengthens the pronoun's ḍamma; Asim and Hamza read a form from tankīs, more emphatic than the common form, while several readers use the second person.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p13/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p13/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p13/r1.claim: ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read “we reverse him” with one vocalization, while others use the alternative; both describe reversing a thing's top and bottom.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p13/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p13/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p13/r2.claim: An extended life reverses the body, strength, youth, reason, and knowledge that had developed from infant weakness into maturity.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p13/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p13/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p13/r3.claim: The reversal returns people toward a child's weakness and lack of understanding; the arrow analogy illustrates turning a thing upside down.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p13/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p13/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p13/r4.claim: The verse echoes the return to decrepit age in 16:70; whoever can reverse human development can also transform people and raise them after death.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p13/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p13/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p13/r5.claim: The interrogative is read with tāʾ by the Medinan, Yaʿqūb, and Sahl readers.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p79/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p79/r10.speaker: نافع وابن ذكوان وأبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p79/r10.claim: They read تعقلون with second-person tāʾ; the remaining canonical readers use third-person yāʾ.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p79/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p79/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p79/r8.claim: God reverses the aging person's creation: initial bodily weakness and lack of reason and knowledge give way to strength, maturity, and understanding, then decline returns him toward childhood's weakness and limited comprehension, like an arrow turned upside down. This proves the power to blind or transform them.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p79/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p79/r9.speaker: عاصم وحمزة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p79/r9.claim: They read ننكسه lightly, while the majority geminate its kāf.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p82/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p82/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p82/r1.claim: The informational statement and interrogative rebuke address Quraysh, urging them away from worshipping idols and toward worship of God.

SAMIN-DURR:36:68/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:68/r1.speaker: عاصم وحمزة
SAMIN-DURR:36:68/r1.claim: Asim and Hamza read ننكسه with a doubled kāf and distinctive vowels, from the intensified نكسه.

SAMIN-DURR:36:68/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:68/r2.speaker: الباقون
SAMIN-DURR:36:68/r2.claim: The remaining readers use the light form, which may convey intensity or not.

SAMIN-DURR:36:68/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:68/r3.speaker: نافع وابن ذكوان
SAMIN-DURR:36:68/r3.claim: As noted earlier in al-Anam, Nafi and Ibn Dhakwan read تعقلون as direct address; the others use third person.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p588/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p588/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p588/r1.claim: As people live longer, they return from strength to weakness and from activity to incapacity, as in 30:54 and 22:5.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p588/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p588/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p588/r2.claim: This world is a place of passage, not permanence; reflecting on life's progression shows people were made for the lasting afterlife.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p276/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p276/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p276/r6.claim: Long life reverses human development: people advance through infancy and maturity, then lose the faculties and knowledge they gained.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p276/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p276/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p276/r7.claim: The doubled reading of nunakkisuhu by ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza points to differing degrees of decline among people.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p276/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p276/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p276/r8.claim: The wording says decline occurs in the created form, avoiding the mistaken implication that God has a created form of His own.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p276/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p276/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p276/r9.claim: Age-related reversal proves God's power to transform creation in reverse as well as to resurrect; its familiarity makes people take it lightly, while rarer transformations seem remote.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p277/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p277/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p277/r1.claim: The common reading addresses people indirectly, while the Madinan readers and Yaʿqūb use direct address, which is more tender and makes the admonition inclusive.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p277/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p277/r2.speaker: بعض العارفين
BIQAI-FULL:v6p277/r2.claim: Some spiritual knowers say “in creation” restricts decline to the body: bodily weakening is inevitable, but knowledge and obedience may grow with age.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p277/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p277/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p277/r3.claim: Ordinary human faculties level off around forty-two; bodily senses stop growing and moral qualities develop only through experience and effort.

DURR-FULL:v7p70/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p70/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p70/r2.claim: Qatada says the reversal in creation is old age, changing hearing, sight, and strength; Ibn Jurayj calls it return to life’s feeblest stage, and Sufyan says eighty years.

DURR-FULL:v7p70/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p70/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p70/r3.claim: Qatada says long life may leave a person unable to know after having known, describing this as old age.

BURSEVI:v7p334#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p334#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p334#2/r1.claim: A long life means extending the period during which the soul animates the body; naks is to turn something upside down, and in creation means reversing the original development into extreme old age.

BURSEVI:v7p334#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p334#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p334#2/r2.claim: The decline progresses through increasing weakness, diminishing strength, failing bodily structure, and changing appearance until the person resembles a child in bodily weakness and loss of understanding and perception.

BURSEVI:v7p334#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p334#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p334#2/r3.claim: A Persian couplet observes that the speaker declines day by day and that nothing escapes decline.

BURSEVI:v7p335/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p335/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p335/r1.claim: If people do not reason from gradual aging, they should infer that its Creator can also efface or transform them outright; such acts are simply not willed in this life.

BURSEVI:v7p335/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p335/r2.speaker: البحر
BURSEVI:v7p335/r2.claim: Al-Bahr says that if such transformations do not occur in this world, they may occur in the next for those who fail to repent, in forms including apes, swine, inverted bodies, blindness, deafness, muteness, and hanging tongues.

BURSEVI:v7p335/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p335/r3.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
BURSEVI:v7p335/r3.claim: Al-Warraq contrasts one aged through heedlessness, whom life’s changing stages affect, with one revived by remembrance, who remains connected to the Real’s life and nearness.

BURSEVI:v7p335/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p335/r4.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v7p335/r4.claim: The verse is a great warning to wake people from heedlessness and make them seize youth and strength for work before they lose the ability.

BURSEVI:v7p335/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p335/r5.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v7p335/r5.claim: The Prophet urged people to seize five blessings before their opposites: youth, health, wealth, life, and free time before old age, illness, poverty, death, and occupation.

BURSEVI:v7p335/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p335/r6.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v7p335/r6.claim: A report says that at ninety God forgives a person, makes him God’s captive on earth, and grants family intercession; at one hundred He refrains from reckoning him, meaning He is pleased and lenient.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#2/r1.claim: Whomever God grants a long life is reversed in bodily development, with steadily increasing weakness and loss of structure and powers.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#2/r2.claim: The image transfers physical reversal to the person's condition by analogy: aging runs opposite to the beginning of life.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#2/r3.speaker: سفيان
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#2/r3.claim: Sufyān says this reversal begins at age eighty.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#2/r4.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects a fixed age of eighty: the onset of weakness varies with temperaments and circumstances.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#2/r5.claim: The clause coordinates with the earlier wish to erase sight as a cause-effect pairing, and serves as evidence for that power.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#2/r6.speaker: جمع من السبعة
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#2/r6.claim: A group of the Seven read nunakkisuhu with a light form, from ankasa.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#2/r7.claim: The question asks whether people see this and still fail to infer that the One who can do it can also erase or transform them; those acts are absent only because God does not will them.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#2/r8.speaker: نافع، ابن ذكوان، أبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v23p46#2/r8.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Dhakwān, and Abū ʿAmr in the ʿAyyāsh transmission read taʿqilūn, second-person address, matching the preceding address.

ELMALILI:36:68-76/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r1.claim: Those granted long lives are turned upside down in their constitution: strength declines and weakness increases as death approaches.

ELMALILI:36:68-76/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r2.claim: People should infer that the power that causes aging could also have transformed people earlier, and so choose the right path.

TABATABAI:36:66-69/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:66-69/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:66-69/r8.claim: A long life reverses human development: strength weakens, increase diminishes, knowledge becomes ignorance, and memory becomes forgetfulness; this demonstrates God's power to blind or transform them.

TABATABAI:36:66-69/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:66-69/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:66-69/r9.claim: The closing question rebukes the audience for failing to reason and urges them to reflect on these signs.

ASAD-NOTES:36:67#n37/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:36:67#n37/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:36:67#n37/r1.claim: People should exercise moral choice promptly because age and growing weakness leave little time.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r5.claim: The punishment-demanders are warned to use their faculties and reason: God can remove sight or deform them, though their respite reflects His mercy.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p401/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p401/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p401/r2.claim: Section IV compares the instantaneous worldly blast with resurrection at the trumpet, portrays judgment and the separate fates, then warns that God can swiftly remove people's abilities; delay is mercy.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p407/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p407/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p407/r4.claim: Human aging is an observable proof that God can reverse and distort human capacities: a newborn is weak, adolescence brings peak strength, and old age returns a person toward helplessness; the Qur'an also describes this arc.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p408/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p408/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p408/r1.claim: Aging returns people to the weakness of childhood as God gradually diminishes their abilities, a general human pattern intensified in old age.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p408/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p408/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p408/r2.claim: Human powers are gifts God may remove, so failing to thank Him and becoming arrogant over them is blameworthy.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p408/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p408/r3.speaker: Most lexicographers
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p408/r3.claim: Most lexicographers treat the two verbs for turning back as synonymous.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p408/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p408/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p408/r4.claim: Islahi argues that the first verb also conveys gradual progression in the reversal, a distinction reflected in both Qur'anic uses.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p408/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p408/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p408/r5.claim: Here khalq means bodily formation or physical shape.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r1.claim: God ends some lives in youth and grants others long life; aging makes the signs of approaching death increasingly visible.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r10.claim: The Qur'an also describes the progressive weakening of bodily and mental abilities in advanced age as life's most feeble stage.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r2.claim: Long life is no guarantee of immortality; aging instead clarifies life's approach to death.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r3.claim: Read with the prior verses, God's ability to end lives young shows He could blind disbelievers or punish them in this world, yet He leaves them free to distinguish right from wrong.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r4.claim: The respite of long life is no future security; disbelievers wrongly treat their limited time as endless capital.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r5.claim: The verse censures disbelievers for failing to reason about these realities.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r6.speaker: Zemahşerî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r6.claim: Old age reverses a person's traits and abilities until he no longer knows what he knew; this demonstrates God's power over the events in verses 66–67.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r7.claim: More broadly, the rebuke may ask why persistent disbelievers do not infer from people's changing states that God can resurrect them after death.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r8.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r8.claim: He reads the verse as criticizing disbelievers for failing to recognize God's ability to resurrect after death.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r9.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:68/r9.claim: God delays punishment for long-lived disbelievers so that persistence in denial and wrongdoing brings them humiliation and defeat.

QIRAAT-ER:36:68:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:36:68:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:36:68:4#1/r1.claim: The Form I reading lacks shadda and makes the reversal simple rather than an intensive causative.

QIRAAT-ER:36:68:9#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:36:68:9#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:36:68:9#1/r1.claim: The second-person plural makes the rebuke direct instead of referring to people in the third person.

STUDYQURAN:36:68/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:68/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:36:68/r1.claim: Long life brings physical and mental decline in old age; this serves as an argument that the One able to cause decline can also resurrect people, as illustrated by the life stages in 30:54 and 22:5.
